questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why Trump and Biden disagree about technology
How hackers changed the result of the 2000 election
How to register to vote in the US
A plan for volunteer hackers to help protect a US election
questions.why: Sam says they'll hear about plans to prevent election cyber-attacks by working with volunteer hackers.

questions.q: Why are US election officials worried about cyber-attacks?
options: Most American voters now vote from abroad by post
Many votes are digital and a lot depends on it
The voting machines in most states are very old
Hackers have already attacked this year's election
questions.why: Rob says many votes are cast digitally, and with so much depending on the result, officials are worried.

questions.q: According to Maya Worman, what harm does interfering with election systems cause?
options: It makes elections much more expensive to run
It delays the final result by several weeks
It weakens the right to vote and public confidence
It stops many young people from voting at all
questions.why: She says interference undermines the right to vote, burdens voters and impacts public confidence.

questions.q: Who is responsible for keeping each area free from cyber-attacks?
options: About eight thousand local jurisdictions
The President's office
A single national agency
The volunteer hackers themselves
questions.why: Sam says it's up to each of the eight thousand local jurisdictions to keep their area safe.

questions.q: What does the Cyber Surge project help with, according to Rob?
options: Counting all the votes by hand after polls close
Choosing new candidates for the local elections
Printing and posting ballot papers to voters
Everything from anti-virus software to big threats
questions.why: Rob says it covers everything from the latest anti-virus software to more serious threats.

questions.q: What worry does Sam raise about the project?
options: It will be too expensive
A troublemaker might sign up as a volunteer
Officials won't listen to the volunteers
Too few people will volunteer
questions.why: Sam asks how we know volunteers are trustworthy, since a troublemaker could sign up.

questions.q: How does Maya Worman answer this worry?
options: Volunteers only give advice and get no sensitive access
Volunteers are watched closely by the police at all times
Volunteers must also work as local election officials
Volunteers are well paid, so they can be fully trusted
questions.why: She says volunteers won't have 'the keys to the castle' but will have a dialogue with administrators.

questions.q: What does Sam hope the project will achieve?
options: More people will vote online
The election will be finished sooner
Everyone will accept the 2020 election result
Hackers will get jobs in government
questions.why: Sam says the 2020 election result will hopefully be accepted by everyone.
